stimulus.text: The engraving, drawn and published by W. Birch & Son in 1799, shows the Bank of the United States in Third Street, Philadelphia: a grand white building with tall columns and a pediment reading “FOUNDED A.D. MDCCXCV.” Carts, horses, and passersby fill the street in front of it.

stem: Which pairing best matches the two parties that formed in the 1790s?

options.text: Federalists: weak central government and farming; Democratic-Republicans: strong central government and trade.
options.misconception: That pairing reverses the two parties’ positions.

options.text: Federalists: pro-French and hostile to banks; Democratic-Republicans: pro-British and friendly to banks.
options.misconception: That pairing reverses the two parties’ positions on France, Britain, and banks.

options.text: Federalists: strong government, commerce, Britain; Democratic-Republicans: farming, states’ rights, France.
Federalists: rule by the states alone; Democratic-Republicans: rule by the president alone.
options.misconception: Background: neither party wanted one level of government to rule alone.

rationales.C: Background: Hamilton led the Federalists toward a strong national government and trade, while Jefferson led the Democratic-Republicans toward farming and strict limits on federal power.
rationales.A: That pairing reverses the two parties’ positions.
rationales.B: That pairing reverses the two parties’ positions on France, Britain, and banks.
rationales.D: Neither party’s program was rule by one level alone.
rationales.general:
1. The engraving shows the bank at the center of Hamilton’s program, an institution his opponents attacked.
2. Background: Hamilton led the Federalists toward a strong national government and trade, while Jefferson led the Democratic-Republicans toward farming and strict limits on federal power.
3. Background: the same split ran through foreign policy, Federalists leaning toward Britain and Democratic-Republicans toward France.
4. So the correct pairing puts commerce, strong government, and Britain on the Federalist side.
Remember: pair the parties by their leaders’ programs, then check the foreign side matches.
